ratings_why.fun: One dial feeds two opposite builds, and the cast order is a real puzzle each turn; Brass, Fanner, Compounder and Pestle Noctuid all stack on the same Phial.
ratings_why.distinct: A deterministic push-your-luck count to an exact number is unlike any tribe today; it still leans on the familiar spell-tribe frame.

verdict_why: The engine is sound, but The Old Lady's reach into fights and Burnished Brass's second cast need clear wording.

points.text: The Old Lady says Once a turn, but Flares can happen in a fight. Say whether she also stops in-fight Flares; it decides whether Lamp in the Fight can run her.
Burnished Brass: say whether the second cast hits the same unit. It changes how Pestle Noctuid and Lamplit Compounder pay out.
A mid-fight Flare drops Heat to 0, which shrinks Six-spot Burnet's Bristle and Eyed Hawk-moth's debuff. That anti-synergy is a nice tension; show it in the build notes so players plan around it.
The Uncertain could make a Phial that Stokes 0 to 2 at random, an uncertain dose that makes the exact-7 count a live choice early.
Skep Pilferer could tie its gold to the Lamp, e.g. gold when you end exactly at the Flashpoint, so it joins one of the builds.

standouts.why: One card that is a safety net for Simmer and a sell decision for Boil Over.
Makes cast order matter: cheap Phials first, then the big spell on the right Moth, and it fights Flaring for the same Heat.
Turns being hit into Heat, so the Lamp can tip over mid-fight and land Burnt-Ring Senior's buff.

weakest.why: Flat gold per cast, no tie to Heat or Flares.
A random target makes it the one Simmer card with no placement choice.
A plain Phial supplier; does its job and nothing else.

flags.note: With Old Carbonaria, the designer's own estimate is 150 to 190 stats a turn.
With Burnished Brass and The Herald, each Phial on a Moth lands twice at high Heat.
Unclear whether Once a turn covers Flares during the fight.
